extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and university faculty (advertising/marketing) seeking A.A.A.A. Educational Foundation research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program rules for research grants awarded by the A.A.A.A. Educational Foundation (1968–1973), including foundation purposes, applicant eligibility, selection criteria, allowable uses, reporting, award size and renewal, and review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation purposes (six major goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Educational Foundation of the American Association of Advertising Agencies was established to foster six major goals: (1) to create a bridge between advertising and university research, (2) to attract top young people to the study of advertising, (3) to raise the academic stature of advertising, (4) to enlarge the body of knowledge about advertising and the consumer, (5) to document the advertising industry's positions with government, and (6) to work toward establishing chairs of advertising at graduate business schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These goals define the program's purpose and the kinds of projects and outcomes the Foundation values (e.g., research that builds academic stature, trains doctoral students, produces publishable knowledge, or serves as credible documentation for policy makers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility: doctoral supervision requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for a grant, a professor had to have one or more doctoral students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility was tied to capacity to support and train doctoral students; the Foundation awarded funds to professors who could provide doctoral research opportunities and help grow the field via student support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection body: Academic Advisory Committee review
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees were selected by an Academic Advisory Committee, appointed by A.A.A.A. and comprised of five distinguished academicians from the fields of economics, liberal arts, advertising education, and graduate business education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals were assessed by academic experts; applicants should expect peer academic evaluation and that criteria reflect scholarly standards as well as applied relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amounts and renewal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded in varying amounts up to $10,000 per year; a renewal for a second year or beyond could be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget proposals should reflect requested amounts up to the program ceiling and include justification for any renewal; successful first-year progress supports renewal requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement and institutional handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant was allocated to the school, but disbursed at the discretion of the grantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional administration receives the award but the principal investigator (grantee) had discretion over spending within program restrictions; applicants should coordinate with their institution on fund handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reporting and evaluation against original proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports were required near the end of the first year, and work accomplished was judged in terms of how closely it related to the original proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must submit progress reports and be prepared that continued funding or renewals depend on demonstrable adherence to the proposed plan and satisfactory progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited and limited uses of grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants could not cover personal compensation of the grantee or school overhead, and not more than 40% of a grant could be used to compensate faculty members not candidates for degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests must exclude PI salary and indirect institutional overhead; faculty compensation paid from the grant is capped (<=40% for faculty who are not degree candidates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 1: Validity and realism of approach
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Validity and realism of approach to proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should present realistic, methodologically sound plans, feasible within the proposed timeline and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 2: Background and accomplishments of proposer and colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Background and accomplishments of professor and colleagues on project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider the PI's and collaborators' prior scholarly record, expertise, and ability to execute the proposed research and supervise students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 3: Freshness and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) Freshness and originality of concept and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority given to innovative research questions or novel methodological approaches that advance understanding in advertising, marketing, communications, or consumer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 4: Potential contribution to disciplinary understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) Potential contributions to understanding of advertising, marketing, communication, or consumer behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate expected substantive contributions (theory, empirical findings, methodological advances) and explain their significance to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 5: Multiplier capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) 'Multiplier' capacity: Will the proposal lead to more doctoral research, published materials, and further study in the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation favored projects that train students, generate publishable outputs, seed additional research programs, or attract further funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 6: Relation to a broader research program
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) Relation to a total research program vs. special individual project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals were evaluated on whether they fit into and strengthen a coherent, sustained research program (preferred) rather than being isolated one-off studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion 7: Supplementary funding
rubrics_metrics.description: (7) Extent to which supplementary funds were provided by the school or other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive proposals demonstrate institutional support or matching funds, indicating local commitment and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of scholarly outputs and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were intended to generate scholarly books, monographs, articles, dissertations, and working papers; program success was judged by published materials and continued research activity stemming from grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose realistic dissemination plans (publications, dissertations) and describe likely short- and long-term impacts on knowledge, policy, or training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on methodological contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The program valued methodological studies that improved measurement sensitivity, validity of instruments, or data analysis procedures applicable across marketing and advertising problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological rigor and contributions that enhance research tools were considered important and could strengthen a proposal's competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for research addressing stages of communications process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation funded research across the Lasswell communications stages (who/source, what/message, whom/audience, which/channel, what effect), including interaction effects and complex causal relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that clearly situate their research within communication-process frameworks and address interactional or multistage effects were aligned with program interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of academic independence and low restriction funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded with a minimum of restrictions to foster academic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Foundation sought to allow academic freedom, the program still required adherence to reporting and budgetary restrictions (e.g., disallowed costs). Proposals should demonstrate responsible use of broadly permissive funding.
